title: PATH-Bench strengthens the historical order/path-dependence closure but does not supply a pre-outcome residual that reopens P15
decision_summary: PATH-Bench substantially strengthens the empirical case that lifelong-agent evaluation is path dependent, including a same-task-set two-path ranking reversal, but its scientific observable remains history-conditioned probe performance and derived transfer/forgetting outcomes. Selective Experience Use introduces a pre-outcome preserve/abstract/ignore control action, not an independently audited order-only uptake/state residual. The paper does not demonstrate a pre-outcome residual that survives a path-integrated continual-learning baseline given the same ordered-history information. Therefore it does not satisfy the requested reopen gate.

historical_p15_provenance.historical_intervention: Hold the same fixed eight-skill set constant and vary only retrieval/presentation order on held-out tasks.
historical_p15_provenance.historical_result: Five evaluable held-out tasks were success-invariant under all six deterministic permutations; the remaining exact-order claim reduced to style/postmortem behavior rather than accepted success conversion.
historical_p15_provenance.historical_reopen_contract: Reopen only if the same fixed skill set is held constant, only presentation/retrieval order changes, and a held-out success residual or independently audited uptake residual remains that static compatibility/negative-transfer baselines cannot express.
historical_p15_provenance.canonicality_note: This historical closure receipt is recoverable from Git history but is not present as an authoritative path on the current origin/main ancestry. It is used here only to reconstruct the prior scientific closure contract, not to overwrite current canonical state.

source_paper.title: PATH-Bench: Path-Dependent Evaluation of Lifelong Agents

requested_reopen_gate.required_for_reopen: A pre-outcome observable or residual produced under a controlled path/order intervention that remains unexplained after a path-integrated continual-learning baseline is given the same ordered-history information.

protocol_level_comparison.pathbench_definition: For ordered history H before probe q, PATH-Bench defines P_q(H) as expected scored performance of the post-history agent on q and calls performance path dependent when P_q(H) varies with the content/order of H.
protocol_level_comparison.p15_mapping: Directly establishes history/order sensitivity of later task performance, but the measured object is the scored probe outcome itself.

protocol_level_comparison.pathbench_definition: Repeated probes are evaluated after controlled positive/negative history intervals; controlled-transition effects are expressed as differences between successive probe-performance measurements such as p_probe_2 - p_probe_1 and p_probe_3 - p_probe_2.
protocol_level_comparison.p15_mapping: Makes path dependence more longitudinal and causally organized than a single endpoint comparison, but still measures downstream performance changes rather than a pre-outcome residual.

protocol_level_comparison.pathbench_definition: A common set of 50 tasks is evaluated under two different task paths; agent rankings in AP/FWT/BWT/FGT change between the two paths.
protocol_level_comparison.p15_mapping: This is strong evidence that order/path matters even when the task set is held fixed. Under the requested gate, this strengthens the old closure/motivation rather than creating a new scientific object.

protocol_level_comparison.pathbench_definition: Agents accumulate past interactions as retrievable memories or reusable skills while traversing task histories.
protocol_level_comparison.p15_mapping: The paper treats this state as the mechanism through which history acts, but it does not define an independently audited order-only state observable whose residual is tested after controlling for the complete ordered history.

protocol_level_comparison.pathbench_definition: Between native retrieval and inference, each retrieved experience is classified for preserve, abstract, or ignore before the task response is produced.
protocol_level_comparison.p15_mapping: SEU is genuinely pre-outcome, but it is an intervention/control policy, not evidence that holding experience content fixed and changing only order yields an independently audited uptake residual. The reported evidence evaluates whether SEU improves AP/FWT/BWT/FGT, again using downstream outcomes.

protocol_level_comparison.pathbench_definition: Directed task relationships are estimated from in-context transfer gains and used to sample helpful/interfering histories.
protocol_level_comparison.p15_mapping: This structures the path intervention but is not a new order-induced pre-outcome agent-state observable.

protocol_level_comparison.pathbench_definition: Multiple lifelong agents and experience representations are compared across controlled histories and outcome metrics.
protocol_level_comparison.p15_mapping: The paper does not provide the requested same-information residual test in which a path-integrated continual-learning baseline receives the full ordered history and then fails to explain an independently measured pre-outcome signal.

substrate_boundary.historical_p15: Within-inference ordering of a fixed retrieved skill set with task and selected content held constant.
substrate_boundary.pathbench: Sequential task ordering over an evolving external learning state accumulated across a lifelong trajectory.
substrate_boundary.implication: The execution substrates are not identical. PATH-Bench is broader and longitudinal, so it should not be described as a literal replication of the historical P15 harness. However, under the explicit requested gate, broader task-path dependence is still insufficient to reopen P15 without the required pre-outcome same-information residual.

strongest_simplification_after_pathbench: Observed path effects can be represented as history-conditioned variation in downstream task performance/transfer/forgetting, together with an explicit experience-use policy such as SEU. PATH-Bench does not establish an additional pre-outcome path-state variable that carries irreducible predictive or causal information once the same ordered history is made available to a path-integrated baseline.
reopen_only_if: A future primary study holds the relevant content/support information fixed, manipulates order/path, measures a pre-outcome uptake/state/decision observable without using the later outcome to define it, and shows a repeatable residual after a strongest path-integrated continual-learning baseline receives the same ordered-history, retrieval/content, task, and lineage information. A same-task-set performance reversal, probe-performance trajectory, or intervention whose benefit is established only through downstream performance is not enough.
